name.text: Matrix addition and subtraction in context (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
[[ if test="is(ctx=1)" ]]

{@nE@} classes keep a record of how many books they borrow from the school library, in {@nC@} categories ({@catStr@}). The numbers borrowed on {@per1@} are given by the matrix \(M\), and those borrowed on {@per2@} by the matrix \(T\).

[[/ if ]][[ if test="is(ctx=2)" ]]

{@nE@} market stalls record how much produce they sell, in {@nC@} types ({@catStr@}). Their sales in kilograms on {@per1@} are given by the matrix \(M\), and on {@per2@} by the matrix \(T\).

[[/ if ]][[ if test="is(ctx=3)" ]]

A shop has {@nElow@} branches that record how many items they sell, in {@nC@} product lines ({@catStr@}). The numbers sold in {@per1@} are given by the matrix \(M\), and in {@per2@} by the matrix \(T\).

[[/ if ]][[ if test="is(ctx=4)" ]]

{@nE@} farms record their harvest, in {@nC@} crops ({@catStr@}). The number of bags harvested {@per1@} is given by the matrix \(M\), and {@per2@} by the matrix \(T\).

[[/ if ]][[ if test="is(ctx=5)" ]]

{@nE@} wildlife conservancies count the animals seen during an annual survey, in {@nC@} species ({@catStr@}). The numbers recorded in {@per1@} are given by the matrix \(M\), and in {@per2@} by the matrix \(T\).

[[/ if ]][[ if test="is(ctx=6)" ]]

{@nE@} clinics record how many patients they see, in {@nC@} services ({@catStr@}). The numbers seen in {@per1@} are given by the matrix \(M\), and in {@per2@} by the matrix \(T\).

[[/ if ]]

\[ M = {@MM@} \qquad T = {@TT@} \]

In each matrix the rows represent {@entStr@}, and the columns represent {@catStr@}, in that order.

(a) Find the total for {@per1@} and {@per2@} combined.

\( M+T = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Find the change from {@per1@} to {@per2@} (that is, \(T-M\)).

\( T-M = \) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
You add (or subtract) two matrices of the same size entry by entry: each entry of the answer comes from the entries in the same position.

(a) Add corresponding entries:

\[ M+T = {@MM@} + {@TT@} = {@sumM@}. \]

(b) Subtract corresponding entries, keeping the order \(T-M\):

\[ T-M = {@TT@} - {@MM@} = {@diffM@}. \]

In part (b) a positive entry is an increase from {@per1@} to {@per2@}, and a negative entry is a decrease.

node.description: Gave the difference T-M instead of the total

truefeedback.text: That is the difference \(T-M\). Part (a) asks for the combined total, so add matching entries: \(M+T\).
It looks like you subtracted. For the total you add the corresponding entries of \(M\) and \(T\).

falsefeedback.text: Not correct. Add each entry of \(M\) to the entry in the same position of \(T\). See the worked solution.

truefeedback.text: You subtracted in the wrong order. The question asks for \(T-M\) (the {@per2@} figures minus the {@per1@} figures), so each entry is (entry of \(T\)) \(-\) (entry of \(M\)).
That is the sum \(M+T\). Part (b) asks for the change, so subtract: \(T-M\).

falsefeedback.text: Not correct. Subtract each entry of \(M\) from the entry in the same position of \(T\). See the worked solution.

qtest.description: (a) gave the difference; (b) reversed the order
